page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 32.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and compression performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.56 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.53 GB/sec, and Passmark memory score at 4334.73. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng registers at an average 16057.94, while Redis SET operations reach 25.37 million operations per second.

Despite strong memory bandwidth and compression speeds, the hardware exhibits specific performance trade-offs. The Passmark CPU encryption test registers as weak at 2358.83, which correlates with the lack of advanced vector, matrix, or complex cryptography instruction flags beyond basic AES. Additionally, while small-model LLM text generation is top-tier at 393.87 tokens/sec for a 135M model, prompt processing for medium 7B models is weak at 22.61 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the integration of 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage directly into a general-purpose ARM64 profile provides high resource density without requiring external storage attachments. This configuration is suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, caching layers like Redis, and lightweight text-generation tasks.
